principles.text: Prefers pullbacks over breakouts because they give tighter risk; skips breakouts already extended from the low of day rather than set a stop 3-5% away.
Gap-up days into index resistance: don't trade the opening-range breakout; wait for a pullback at least into the anchored VWAP, ideally into clustered/converging EMAs.
Crypto names move fast, so he enters more aggressively on the shorter timeframe (e.g., hourly 9 pullback) rather than waiting for a close above the daily 9; the 21 EMA is the key support to watch.
Several names from the same theme on the same day are each still sized ~20-25%; a re-entry after a stop uses the same size, so a tighter stop means less account risk (MSTR re-entry ~0.15%).
Tight stops raise reward/risk and control risk but get taken out easily; they require a pinpoint entry and punish chasing.
No price targets; exits on volume expansion, price acceleration, or a failure of a defined EMA.
Watchlists re-split by daily dollar volume (>$500M vs $100-500M); concentrate on the liquid names, since sub-$500M names bring slippage and wider spreads.
Edge = finding asymmetric risk/reward entries, whatever the tactic; expects tactics to decay and to adapt.

Entry windows in this tape are short (Thursday/Friday gave the best entries); with QQQ/SPY stretched above the EMAs, the priority now is to stop entering new trades, avoid FOMO, and wait for a pullback into the daily 9 while sitting tight.
Book some profits into an index gap-up into resistance (QQQ at top of gap, Russell into declining 9).
